messages:
maria-sec: FYI — customer request: private deployment in their VPC, fully segmented, air-gapped option. They asked for a hard isolation checklist (RBAC delta, audit forwarding, KMS integration, egress constraints). Can we triage gaps and list must-haves?

tj-infra: +1. Quick questions: are we allowing hostNetwork / hostPID for any infra pods? also need to confirm conntrack/conntrack max settings and kube-proxy mode.

kevin-ml: For model weights: customer requires envelope encryption with customer-managed keys (BYOK). Do we support wrapping model artifacts with their KMS?

sara-platform: We do KMS envelope currently via our storage gateway but not with external HSM-backed keys in the private bundle. We can wire KMS endpoint config in the private control plane; rotation flow needs to be documented.

oncall-bot: [alert] CVE-2024-XXXX: kubelet unauthenticated read on hostPaths - advisory posted. See https://sec.example.com/CVE-2024-XXXX

maria-sec: Good catch. For isolation guarantees I propose: disallow hostNetwork and hostPID by default; only allow hostPath mounts via an explicit whitelist and only read-only. Also require PSP-equivalent admission (OPA Gatekeeper) to validate allowed mounts.

tj-infra: Agreed. I'll draft a quick NetworkPolicy template for the serving namespace and a recommended egress proxy rule. Example network policy we can use as a baseline:

```
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: redwood-serving-egress-lockdown
  namespace: redwood-serving
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes: ["Egress"]
  egress:
    - to:
      - ipBlock:
          cidr: 10.0.0.0/16
      ports:
      - protocol: TCP
        port: 443
    - to:
      - podSelector:
          matchLabels:
            component: kube-dns
      ports:
      - protocol: UDP
        port: 53
```

kevin-ml: For KMS, customer wants a path where the model server decrypts ephemeral keys from their KMS and we never persist plaintext. Implementation idea: startup agent fetches a short-lived envelope key from their KMS, writes it to memory-only volume and uses it to unwrap weights. We should confirm our runtime supports memfd/ramfs in the private package.

sara-platform: We support tmpfs mounts in our on-prem installer but need to document kernel constraints. Also will add HSM connector config (PKCS#11) to the control plane config.

maria-sec: Audit logging: they require immutable audit stream to a customer-owned SIEM via TLS with mutual auth. We need to expose fluentd/collector config in the private bundle and ensure audit logs include request.user, verb, resource, namespace, and ABAC not used. Also retention/rotation guidance.

oncall-bot: [note] playbook link: /playbooks/private-deploy-audit-forwarding.md

tj-infra: Quick vuln triage notes: 1) Block hostNamespace mounts 2) Enforce seccomp/defaultDrop 3) Limit capabilities (no NET_ADMIN) 4) OPA/Gatekeeper policy to prevent new ClusterRoleBindings without security review.

kevin-ml: Any implications on latency if we add an egress proxy for KMS calls? customer is sensitive to p99 latency for token refresh. We might need endpoint affinity and local caching of unwrapping tokens.

maria-sec: Action items: 
- tj-infra: produce NPolicy + egress-proxy pattern + gatekeeper constraint (ETA EOD tomorrow)
- sara-platform: KMS/HSM connector doc + installer flags for tmpfs + mTLS config (ETA 2 business days)
- kevin-ml: verify model server can operate with ephemeral in-memory key wrap and write a short integration test (ETA 3 days)
- maria-sec: draft a minimal audit-forwarding template and required audit fields (ETA tomorrow)

sara-platform: For RBAC changes: recommend forbidding creation of ClusterRoleBinding via webhook unless requestor in group:sec-admins. Example Gatekeeper constraint we can reuse. Also add an approval step in console UI for private installs.

tj-infra: I'll include kubectl commands for triage and quick mitigation:

```
# list any pods running hostNetwork
kubectl get pods --all-namespaces -o json | jq '.items[] | select(.spec.hostNetwork==true) | {ns:.metadata.namespace, name:.metadata.name}'

# lock down a namespace with NetworkPolicy
kubectl apply -f redwood-serving-networkpolicy.yaml
```

maria-sec: Incident response notes: if there's a suspected hostPath exploit, isolate node, collect /var/log/kubelet logs, rotate node certificates, and revoke credentials. Use our private-controlplane to revoke service account tokens via token controller and rotate KMS keys if compromise suspected.

kevin-ml: I'll add an eval to the CI that spins up a private bundle and validates no hostPath, no hostNetwork, and that KMS unwrap path works with ephemeral key.

maria-sec: Great. Let's reconvene after PRs. If anyone sees blockers ping @maria-sec and add to the incident channel if it's an active CVE. :lock: :shield:
